Chapter 7: The Influence of Authority and the Power of Obedience
Have you ever thought of yourself as someone who always follows your own values and instincts? Most of us do. But, the moment someone in charge steps in, everything can shift—sometimes without us even noticing.
Imagine starting a brand-new job. You want to make a good impression, right? Now, suppose your boss asks you to stay late, even though it means missing something important at home. You hesitate for a second, but the urge to say yes is almost automatic. You agree, telling yourself it’s just this one time. Later, your mind comes up with reasons to justify that choice, helping you smooth over any guilt or discomfort.
This urge to obey authority is surprisingly strong, and it often works beneath the surface. There’s a famous experiment where people were told to give what they thought were painful electric shocks to someone else, just because a person in a lab coat told them to. Even when they felt uneasy, most went along with it. Their respect for authority actually overpowered their own values—and even their empathy.
But here’s the thing: authority’s influence isn’t just about dramatic experiments or big moments. It’s woven into everyday life—in the way we follow rules, accept what experts say, or automatically listen to people with impressive titles. Our minds tend to assume that those in charge know best...even if deep down, we have our doubts.
Sometimes, this trust in authority is a good thing. It helps groups work together and makes decisions move faster. But it can also backfire. When we stop questioning orders or just go along with what’s expected, we risk giving up our own judgment—and sometimes, that leads to mistakes or even harm.
The relationship between our minds and authority is complicated. We want to be seen as cooperative and respectful, but we also want to feel independent. That push and pull shapes so many choices, whether we realize it or not.
So, what can we do? The first step is just noticing how powerful authority can be. By asking questions, looking for different points of view, and trusting our own sense of right and wrong, we can push back against the urge to blindly obey. Authority will always have an effect on us—but with a little awareness, we get to decide when to follow...and when it’s time to stand our ground.
